```{r}
#| label: setup

source("../_common.R")
```

I got pretty excited when I saw Posit's [blog post](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-09-30_introducing-shinyreact/) announcing the `shinyreact` package. I've worked on a few [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) apps, but couldn't really wrap my head around how a Shiny and [React](https://react.dev/) R package would work.

I recently built a Shiny app-package for browsing [#TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) datasets: `ttdviewer`. I designed the UI so I could pick a dataset title, view the files in List, Summary, and Graphs (from [`inspectdf`](https://alastairrushworth.com/inspectdf/)). I can also download one file or all of a dataset's files as CSV or `parquet`. You can view the documentation and code for `ttdviewer` on its [site](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/ttdviewer/). 

`ttdviewer` uses `bslib` (`page_sidebar()`, `sidebar()`, and `navset_tab()`). In this post I'll cover converting the UI to [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/), the parts of the conversion the documentation doesn't cover, and the few surprises I hit along the way.

## What is `shinyreact`?

`shinyreact` moves the UI *out* of R. The server still holds the reactive graph (`input`, `reactive()`, `req()`, and `bindEvent()` all behave as usual), but the page is a React client we write ourselves. 

The diagram below gives a broad overview of how React works and how `shinyreact` supplies the plumbing between the React UI and the reactive server:

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-align: 'center'
```

`shinyreact` is pretty new (version 0.1.0), and the documentation calls it a pre-release, so it's not on CRAN:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r")
```

The R side is small. The package exports seven functions, and `ttdviewer` only uses two of them (`page_react()` and `reactive_output()`):

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
ls("package:shinyreact")
#> [1] "page_bare"       "page_react"      "page_react_dep"  "page_react_html"
#> [5] "reactive_output" "send_message"    "wire_tap"
```

1. `page_react()` replaces the UI function and serves a `ui.js` (and `ui.css`) from `src_dir`. The server sends no body HTML, so the client creates its own mount point. The other `page_*` functions cover setups `page_react()` doesn't:    
    * `page_react_html()`: serves a complete `index.html` (the kind a Vite build writes) and injects the Shiny dependencies into it.   
    * `page_react_dep()`: builds the `htmltools::htmlDependency()` for a bundle. `page_react()` calls it for us.    
    * `page_bare()`: a bare page with jQuery and Shiny (and no Bootstrap unless we pass a `theme`).   
2. `reactive_output()` sends any R value to the client as JSON. The client reads it with `useShinyOutputValue()`.   
3. `send_message()` pushes a custom message from the server to a React component, which receives it with `useShinyMessageHandler()`. The message id is namespaced like an input or output id, so it works inside modules.   
4. `wire_tap()` is for testing. It reads the JSON that crossed the Shiny websocket during a `shinytest2` run, so tests can check what the server actually sent to the client.

### Client hooks

On the client, the hooks on `window.shinyreact` read and write Shiny values: `useShinyInput()` sets `input[[id]]`, `useShinyOutputValue()` reads a `reactive_output()`, and `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput` host classic Shiny outputs inside React. `ShinyModuleProvider` namespaces the hook ids, so Shiny modules still work.

The diagram below shows how values move between the two sides:

## Spike first

Before touching the package, I asked Claude to build a spike (small prototype) to test each output with the Netflix Titles data (one file) and Space Launches data (two files).

### The prompt

The `shinyreact` documentation only shows R examples for `plotly` and `reactable`. `ttdviewer` also uses `listviewerlite`, `renderPlot()`, and `downloadHandler()`, and the client has to be served from an installed package. The prompt asked the spike to answer those questions and nothing else:

```{verbatim}
Before we convert ttdviewer to shinyreact, build a throwaway spike outside
the repo. Use shinyreact 0.1.0 from GitHub and the no build pattern
(page_react() serving www/ui.js). Load ttdviewer with load_all() and test
the outputs the shinyreact docs don't cover:

1. listviewerlite::listview() through renderUI()
2. inspect_plot() through renderPlot()
3. downloadHandler() for CSV and zip downloads
4. reactable (documented, but confirm it works with our data)

Use Netflix Titles (one file) and Space Launches (two files). Then check
that page_react() can serve the client from an installed package
(inst/www/). Report what works, what breaks, and why.
```

### The structure

The spike is just two files. There's no build step: `page_react()` finds `www/ui.js`, and the client uses `React.createElement()` (aliased as `h()`) instead of JSX.

::: {style="font-style: italic;"}

```{verbatim}
spike
├── app.R
└── www
    └── ui.js

2 directories, 2 files
```

:::

`app.R` loads `ttdviewer` with `load_all()` and defines one output for each question in the prompt:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: 'show/hide app.R'
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)
pkgload::load_all("~/projects/apps/R/ttdviewer", quiet = TRUE)

ui <- page_react(theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  data <- reactive({
    req(input$title)
    load_tt_data(input$title)
  })

  # i. plain values for the client
  output$titles <- reactive_output(sort(unique(all_tt_combined$title)))

  output$files <- reactive_output({
    if (is.null(input$title)) return(NULL)
    d <- data()
    list(names = names(d), date = format(attr(d[[1]], "date")))
  })

  # ii. listviewerlite (HTML)
  output$list <- renderUI({
    req(data())
    listviewerlite::listview(data())
  })

  # iii. reactable (htmlwidget)
  output$table <- reactable::renderReactable({
    req(data())
    reactable::reactable(utils::head(data()[[1]], 1000), searchable = TRUE)
  })

  # iv. inspect_plot() ggplot
  output$plt_types <- renderPlot({
    req(data())
    inspect_plot(data()[1], plots = "types")
  })

  # v. download
  output$download <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() tt_download_filename(data(), input$format, input$title),
    content = function(file) write_tt_download(data(), input$format, file)
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`ui.js` reads the plain values with `useShinyOutputValue()`, sends the title and format back with `useShinyInput()`, and hosts the classic outputs in `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput`:

```{verbatim}
const {
  React, ReactDOM, useShinyInput, useShinyOutputValue, ShinyOutput, ImageOutput,
} = window.shinyreact;
const h = React.createElement;

function App() {
  const titles = useShinyOutputValue("titles", []);
  const files = useShinyOutputValue("files", null);
  const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("title", "Netflix Titles");
  const [format, setFormat] = useShinyInput("format", "csv");

  return h("div", { className: "container py-3" },
    h("select", { id: "title", className: "form-select mb-2", value: title,
      onChange: (e) => setTitle(e.target.value) },
      titles.map((t) => h("option", { key: t, value: t }, t))),
    files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", files.names.join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date),
    h("select", { className: "form-select mb-2", value: format,
      onChange: (e) => setFormat(e.target.value) },
      ["csv", "parquet", "original"].map((f) => h("option", { key: f, value: f }, f))),
    h(ShinyOutput, { id: "download", tagName: "a", className: "btn btn-primary shiny-download-link",
      href: "", target: "_blank", download: "" }, "Download"),
    h("h4", { className: "mt-3" }, "List"),
    h(ShinyOutput, { id: "list", className: "shiny-html-output" }),
    h("h4", null, "Table"),
    h(ShinyOutput, { id: "table", className: "reactable html-widget html-widget-output",
      "data-reactable-output": "table" }),
    h("h4", null, "Plot"),
    h(ImageOutput, { id: "plt_types", width: "100%", height: "300px" }),
  );
}

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"))).render(h(App));
```

### The outputs

Every output worked once the client was fixed (see [Surprises](#surprises-in-the-spike) below). The rest of this section covers how each one is hosted on the client.

#### Lists

`listviewerlite::listview()` returns HTML, so the server keeps `renderUI()`, and the client hosts it with the `shiny-html-output` class:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$list <- renderUI({
  req(data())
  listviewerlite::listview(data())
})
```

```{verbatim}
h(ShinyOutput, { id: "list", className: "shiny-html-output" }),
```

#### Tables

`reactable` works the documented way: a `ShinyOutput` with the widget classes (`reactable html-widget html-widget-output`).

#### Plots

`ImageOutput` is only documented for Python, but it follows the same contract as R's `renderPlot()`. The client reports its size through `.clientdata_output_<id>_width` and `_height`, and draws the image `renderPlot()` sends back. The `inspect_plot()` ggplots rendered unchanged:

```{verbatim}
h(ImageOutput, { id: "plt_types", width: "100%", height: "300px" }),
```

#### Downloads

`downloadHandler()` binds to an anchor with the `shiny-download-link` class, so a `ShinyOutput` with `tagName="a"` works:

```{verbatim}
h(ShinyOutput, { id: "download", tagName: "a", className: "btn btn-primary shiny-download-link",
  href: "", target: "_blank", download: "" }, "Download"),
```

The CSV download for Netflix Titles returned 3.0 MB, and the two file zip for Space Launches returned 104 KB.

#### Packaging

`page_react()` passes `src_dir` to `page_react_dep()`, which builds an `htmltools::htmlDependency()` with a file source. I wanted to see if the file sources work from an installed package, which I confirmed by installing a copy of `ttdviewer` with `ui.js` in `inst/www/` into a temporary library:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
app_ui <- function() {
  shinyreact::page_react(
    useBusyIndicators(spinners = TRUE, pulse = TRUE),
    src_dir = system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer"),
    theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),
    title = "#TidyTuesday Viewer"
  )
}
```

* `system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer")` found `ui.js`, and `page_react_dep()` built a `type="module"` script from it. So the built client belongs in `inst/www/`.

* `bs_theme(version = 5)` keeps Bootstrap on the page, so the React components can use the same classes (`form-select`, `nav-tabs`, `card`) the `bslib` UI used.

### Surprises {#surprises-in-the-spike}

The spike turned up two small surprises and one crash. `ImageOutput` worked with R's `renderPlot()` (see Plots above). And `reactable` didn't need a `reactableOutput()` placeholder, because `shinyreact` finds the widget's JavaScript from the render function. The crash came from a plain value.

#### Length one vectors

`reactive_output()` passes the R value through unchanged, and Shiny serializes it with `auto_unbox`, so a character vector of length one arrives as a string, not an array.

In `app.R`, `output$files` sends the file names and the TidyTuesday date for the selected title, and `ui.js` joins the names into a single line with `files.names.join(", ")`.

The spike's default title was Netflix Titles, which has one file. The app crashed on load, and the browser console showed:

```{verbatim}
TypeError: files.names.join is not a function
    at App (http://127.0.0.1:8765/spike-1795455972/ui.js:16:61)
    at vf (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:47833)
    at Yf (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:70472)
    at Gd (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:80765)
    at ry (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:116187)
    at Kr (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115267)
    at uc (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115104)
    at cy (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:111963)
    at My (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:123483)
    at It (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:17:1579)
```

Shiny's internal `toJSON()` shows why. One file arrives as a string, and two files arrive as an array:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# one file (Netflix Titles)
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("netflix_titles.csv")))
#> {"names":"netflix_titles.csv"}
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# two files (Space Launches)
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("agencies.csv", "launches.csv")))
#> {"names":["agencies.csv","launches.csv"]}
```

#### The fix

The spike fixed the client line with `[].concat()`, which turns a string into a one element array and leaves an array alone:

```{verbatim}
files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", [].concat(files.names).join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date),
```

We can also protect the vector on the server with `I()`, which keeps it an array:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = I("netflix_titles.csv")))
#> {"names":["netflix_titles.csv"]}
```

Or we can wrap it on the client, so every `reactive_output()` is covered. In the package, I went with a small client helper:

```{verbatim}
export function asArray<T>(x: T | T[] | null | undefined): T[] {
  if (x === null || x === undefined) return [];
  return Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x];
}
```

## The conversion

The conversion lives on its own branch, so `main` keeps the `bslib` app. The spike was built outside the repo, so the branch starts with the full conversion in one commit (`convert UI to shinyreact`). The graph below shows how the two branches diverge:

The branches don't share UI code anymore, so every change happens twice. I've added a few improvements to both (reordering the tabs, clearer graph labels, and the option to download one file or all files). I haven't decided if I will merge the two branches, but for now I've updated the documentation in each branch to describe the changes.

### The client

`npm run build` writes `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`:

::: {style="font-style: italic;"}

```{verbatim}
js/
├── package-lock.json
├── package.json
├── src
│   ├── components
│   │   ├── DatasetSelect.tsx
│   │   ├── Download.tsx
│   │   ├── GraphsTab.tsx
│   │   ├── ListTab.tsx
│   │   ├── SummaryTab.tsx
│   │   └── TitleInput.tsx
│   ├── shinyreact.ts
│   ├── ui.css
│   └── ui.tsx
├── tsconfig.json
└── vite.config.ts
```

:::

React isn't bundled, because `shinyreact.js` (served by the R package) already provides it, so Vite maps `react` to the global `shinyreact.React`:

```{verbatim}
rollupOptions: {
  external: ["react"],
  output: { globals: { react: "shinyreact.React" } },
},
```

`js/` is in `.Rbuildignore`, and the built bundle is committed, so installing the package doesn't require Node.

The path from source files to the browser looks like this:

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-align: 'center'

    Build[["<code>npm run build</code><br>(Vite)"]]
    WWW[("<code>inst/www/</code><br><code>ui.js</code> + <code>ui.css</code>")]

    Src -->|"i. compile"| Build
```

### What happened to the modules?

All the module UI functions are gone. The server module functions keep their `id`s, and the client wraps the matching component in a `ShinyModuleProvider` with the same namespace:

```{verbatim}
<ShinyModuleProvider namespace="input">
  <TitleInput />
</ShinyModuleProvider>
```

The namespace strings on the client have to match the module ids in `app_server()`:

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-align: 'center'
```

### Plain values

Plain values (the dataset titles, file names, and the Summary file overview) moved to `reactive_output()`. For example, `mod_input_server()` used to get its choices from `selectInput()` in the UI module. Now it sends them:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$titles <- shinyreact::reactive_output(
  unique(all_tt_combined$title[!is.na(all_tt_combined$data_files)])
)
```

And `TitleInput.tsx` reads the titles and sends the selection back as `input$ds_title`:

```{verbatim}
const titles = asArray(useShinyOutputValue<string | string[]>("titles", []));
const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("ds_title", "Space Launches");
```

The table below maps each module to its outputs and client component:

| Module | R output | Client |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_input` | `titles` (`reactive_output()`) | `TitleInput.tsx` |
| `mod_download` | `files` (`reactive_output()`); `download` (`downloadHandler()`) | `Download.tsx` |
| `mod_list` | `list` (`renderUI()`) | `ListTab.tsx` |
| `mod_summary` | `overview`, `choices` (`reactive_output()`); `stats`, `vars`, `table` (`renderReactable()`) | `SummaryTab.tsx` |
| `mod_plot` | `datasets` (`reactive_output()`); `plt_<type>` (`renderPlot()`) | `GraphsTab.tsx` |

### Plot outputs

The plot module changed the most. The `bslib` version populated a dataset `selectInput()` with `updateSelectInput()`, created `renderPlot()` calls inside an observer, and built the plot containers with `renderUI()`. It also piped `return(...)` into `bindEvent()`, so the `bindEvent()` never ran.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# mod_plot_server() from main branch
observe({ #<1>
  if (is.null(ttd_r())) {
    updateSelectInput(session, "dataset", choices = character(0))
    return()
  }
  ds <- names(ttd_r())
  updateSelectInput(session, "dataset", choices = ds, selected = ds[[1]])
}) |>
  bindEvent(ttd_r(), ignoreNULL = FALSE) #<1>

observe({ #<2>
  ds_list <- req(ttd_r())
  sel_ds  <- input$dataset
  req(sel_ds %in% names(ds_list))
  df <- ds_list[[sel_ds]]
  purrr::walk(input$plots, function(plt) {
    output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({
      inspect_plot(ttd = setNames(list(df), sel_ds), plots = plt)
    })
  })
}) |>
  bindEvent(list(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots), ignoreNULL = TRUE) #<2>

output$plots_ui <- renderUI({ #<3>
  req(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots)
  purrr::map(input$plots, function(plt) {
    tagList(
      h4(names(plot_labels())[plot_labels() == plt]),
      plotOutput(ns(paste0("plt_", plt)), height = "300px")
    )
  })
}) #<3>

return( #<4>
  reactive({
    list("dataset" = input$dataset, "plots" = input$plots)
  })
) |>
  bindEvent(list(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots), ignoreNULL = TRUE) #<4>
```
1. Populate the dataset dropdown once ttd is available  
2. Render each selected plot type for chosen dataset  
3. Dynamically generate UI for selected plot types
4. `return()` exits before `bindEvent()` runs

The new version creates one `renderPlot()` per plot type up front, and each one is gated by `req()`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
purrr::walk(PLOT_TYPES, function(plt) {
  output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({
    req(plt %in% input$plots)
    ds <- selected() #<1> 
    tryCatch(
      inspect_plot(ttd = ds, plots = plt),
      error = function(err) {
        plot.new()
        text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red")
      }
    )
  })
})
```
1. outside `tryCatch()` so `req()` is not caught as an error

The checkboxes and plot containers now live in `GraphsTab.tsx`, and `PLOT_TYPES` has to match in both places.

## Surprises in the conversion

The conversion turned up two more surprises.

### Outputs that never rendered

`app_server()` has a `dev` output (a `listview()` of the reactive values) in a closed `<details>` element in the sidebar. In the `bslib` UI it never rendered. Inside React it does, and `listviewerlite::listview()` errors on `NULL` elements (before a title loads). It now drops them with `purrr::compact()`.

### No type to search

The title picker is a native `<select>`, so it lost the type to search behavior `selectize` gave `selectInput()`. With 432 titles that's noticeable, and it's the main thing I'm still deciding on.

## Recap

The spike helped discover what a `shinyreact` conversion would look like: 

1. The server would barely change.  
2. The server module functions would keep their ids. 
3. `downloadHandler()`, `renderPlot()`, `renderUI()`, and `renderReactable()` would all work inside React, and the busy indicators still show. 

Conceptually, I had to wrap my head around the new UI location (`js/` builds into `inst/www/`), and how the plain values get to it (`reactive_output()`). 

The test suite dropped from 178 to 164, because the UI module tests were dropped with the functions they tested.

I'll keep the conversion on the `shinyreact` branch for now, because I haven't decided if I will merge it. `shinyreact` is pre-release, so a merge would need the `pkgdown` GitHub Action to install it from `Remotes`, and a decision on the title picker.
